assessment_summary: I validated the documented venv/editable installation (adapted to Linux per the summary) by inspecting artifacts and exercising real behavior. The package is registered as an editable install (`pip show` -> pomodoro-timer 0.3.0, location /workspace), its dependencies (PySide6 6.11.2, shiboken6) are installed, and the console entry point /workspace/.venv/bin/pomodoro resolves to pomodoro.cli:main in the source tree. Running the installed command both as `.venv/bin/pomodoro` and `python -m pomodoro` with QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen kept the Qt event loop running until an 8s timeout (exit 124), demonstrating successful startup without errors; no X server exists so offscreen was used (xvfb absent). The repo test suite passed 20/20. A real offscreen `MainWindow` instantiated, showed visible, exposed the documented `Timer`/`Statistik` tabs, Start/Abbrechen/History-reset buttons, and German statistics labels. Runtime data files (settings.json and pomodoro.db with the focus_sessions schema) are created in the per-OS data dir. Critically, I reproduced the software's defining feature end-to-end through the actual GUI engine: a completed focus round was written as duration=1.0/completed=1, and a focus round aborted at 30s was recorded as duration=0.5/completed=0, confirming interrupted sessions are honestly counted as the guide states. The missing-sound path degrades gracefully (returns False, no crash). Limitations: macOS-only deliverables (PyInstaller .app, build.sh, code signing) and the Docker/noVNC alternative were not part of the performed method and their absence does not indicate failure; MP3 sounds and POMODORO_* overrides were intentionally unset. All observed evidence supports a complete, operational installation.
